clue.text: My corrupted README file, with missing line, failing to open

indicators.note: a corrupted file has its contents scrambled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the shortened word fails at its opening, so its first letter goes
the file is shown missing something, so that letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Someone groans that a damaged README document, already short a line, now won't even open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing line' takes L from FILE to leave FIE; 'failing to open' drops its first letter, leaving IE. README plus IE is rearranged, signalled by 'corrupted'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of dismay, as in 'My!' or 'Oh dear!', so the old-fashioned interjection swaps in.

clue.text: Outlaw in favour of offer

parts.note: being for something is being in favour of it
a bid is an offer, as at an auction

explanation.surface: A legal ban that is somehow in favour of an offer, like a contradictory law.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw something is to prohibit it, the verb sense rather than the noun for a criminal.

clue.text: Extract from Hungarian melody

indicators.note: an extract is a piece taken out of the word Hungarian, so the letters sit inside it

explanation.surface: A passage lifted from a Hungarian tune, perhaps by Liszt or Bartók.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera, a tune for one voice.

clue.text: It crosses Scotland or Canada, all on nice loco

indicators.note: loco is slang for crazy, so the letters of the words before it go mad and rearrange

explanation.surface: A puzzle over whether a railway line crosses Scotland or Canada, with everyone aboard a pleasant locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like a train engine, matching the travel picture; here it means crazy. The Caledonian Canal runs from Inverness to Fort William through the Great Glen.
explanation.definitionFit: This waterway cuts right across the Highlands, linking the North Sea side to the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: On the face of it, success is targeted in the fewest possible turns

definitions.text: On the face of it, success is targeted in the fewest possible turns

parts.words: On the face of it, success is targeted in the fewest possible turns
parts.note: the puzzle is solved one face at a time by twisting its layers, and speed-solvers aim for the fewest moves

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the face of it' sounds like 'apparently', but the faces are literal: coloured squares on each side of a puzzle solved by twisting.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous colourful puzzle is solved by twisting layers until each face shows one colour, and enthusiasts compete on move counts.

clue.text: Evidently immodest about quashing international flare-up

indicators.note: the reversed phrase squashes the letter into its middle, holding it inside
about here signals turning round, so the phrase is read backwards

parts.note: someone plainly immodest is evidently not pure

explanation.surface: Someone shamelessly immodest is on the point of crushing an international outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns NOT PURE round to ERUPTON, and 'quashing' puts I inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: An eruption is a sudden outbreak, such as of violence or a volcano, just as a flare-up is.

clue.text: Hope a lord will seize power

indicators.note: the lord's letters grab hold of the power letter and hold it within

parts.note: sire is an old form of address for a lord or king
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: A hope that a nobleman will mount a coup and grab power.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to aim or long for something, so it means to hope, as a verb.

clue.text: Artist on the subject of film genre

parts.note: re means concerning, about
noir is the genre of dark crime thrillers, film noir

explanation.surface: A painter discussing the topic of film noir.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was a French Impressionist painter, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Tank curator is inspired by a couple of pints

indicators.note: inspired here means breathed in, so the letters go inside the following word

parts.note: a quart is two pints
taken as written

explanation.surface: A museum keeper of tanks gets inspiration from a pair of pints at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tank curator' suggests a military museum, but the tank holds fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An aquarist keeps an aquarium, looking after the fish and their water.

clue.text: Tease bishop in prison game

indicators.note: the teasing and the bishop go inside the prison word

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement, a prison
to rib someone is to tease them
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Mocking a jailed churchman with a game, like a prison scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Cribbage is a card game scored by moving pegs along a board.

clue.text: Injure husband and wife on westbound major route

indicators.note: in an across answer, one part on another means it comes after it
in an across clue, going west means reading right to left, so the letters are turned

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, written M I with the figure as the letter
a married couple is a pair

explanation.surface: A married couple get hurt while travelling west on a big motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or weaken it, much as to injure it.

clue.text: Lying in coma, due out before 1st of September

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come before the next one in the answer
out means wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
the first letter of the word September

explanation.surface: Someone is lying comatose, with release due before the start of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lying' looks like lying in a coma; it is the definition, meaning dishonest.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendacious means untruthful, given to telling falsehoods.

clue.text: Set up tent — coitus unfolds

indicators.note: unfolding opens things out and changes their shape, so the letters rearrange

explanation.surface: Pitching a tent, then lovemaking takes place inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To constitute an organisation is to establish or found it formally.

clue.text: Rebecca and I swapped animal

indicators.note: the two pieces change places, so the letter I moves to the front

parts.note: Bex is a pet form of the name Rebecca

explanation.surface: Rebecca and the speaker trade places, or perhaps trade pets.
explanation.definitionFit: An ibex is a wild mountain goat with long curved horns.

clue.text: Controversial bias set in stone ends badly around university

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the university letter
the words are put together badly, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A prejudice carved in stone finishes poorly at a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendentiousness is a partisan slant in writing or argument, promoting a disputed point of view.

clue.text: Decline getting into calamitous European fight

indicators.note: the decline word goes into the calamity word

parts.note: dire means dreadful, calamitous
to sag is to sink or decline

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to join a disastrous European conflict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like the definition (refuse); it is the piece, and the definition is 'fight'.
explanation.definitionFit: To disagree is to argue or quarrel, a mild sense of fighting with someone.

clue.text: Turn back short old maid

parts.note: to spin is to turn

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the stern is the back of a ship

explanation.surface: A curt old servant is told to turn round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old maid' suggests a servant; it is an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Old maid is a dated term for an older woman who never married, as is spinster.

clue.text: Dauphins regularly used honeybees

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals, every second one of Dauphins

explanation.surface: French princes routinely made use of honeybees.
explanation.definitionFit: Apis is the scientific genus name of the honeybees.

clue.text: Face character overseas, former Albanian king

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, a foreign character
Zog I was King of Albania from 1928 to 1939

explanation.surface: A portrait of a foreign figure, the old Albanian king.
explanation.definitionFit: Phizog is jocular British slang for a person's countenance, from physiognomy.

clue.text: Cut offer by accepting terms in legal promo

indicators.note: the offer takes on the following letters at its end

parts.note: to tender is to offer

indicators.note: terms are ends, here the final letters of legal and promo

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reduced bid on condition of agreed terms in a lawful advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a reduction; it is a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is a prime cut of beef or pork from the loin.

clue.text: Nearly sick following fast pulse

indicators.note: the sick word comes after the fast word

parts.note: Lent is the Christian period of fasting

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell after a period of not eating, with a quickened heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulse' looks like a heartbeat; here it is an edible seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is a legume, and pulses are the edible seeds of such plants.

clue.text: Move restlessly, following unintroduced thingamyjig

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: without its introduction, so the first letter is left off

parts.note: a widget is any small gadget whose name escapes you

explanation.surface: Squirming about while chasing some nameless gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: To fidget is to make small restless movements, unable to keep still.

clue.text: Caution adult Scotsman for breaking crockery

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the Scotsman breaks into the crockery word, sitting inside it

parts.note: a dish is an item of crockery
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A grown Scot is warned off for smashing plates.
explanation.definitionFit: To admonish someone is to warn or reprimand them, as a verb meaning caution.

clue.text: Different cardinals once acting gently

indicators.note: different means changed, so the numeral letters are put in another order

parts.note: cardinal numbers as the Romans once wrote them: four numerals, 1000, 500, 50 and 1, listed largest first

explanation.surface: Former cardinals behaving tenderly in a variety of ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cardinals' suggests churchmen; here they are cardinal numbers written as Roman numerals, rearranged into a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mild describes behaviour that is gentle and not harsh.

clue.text: Rambling tirade on furry creatures

indicators.note: rambling means wandering about, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A long-winded rant about fluffy animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodentia is the zoological order of gnawing mammals such as rats, mice and squirrels.

clue.text: Biden's example of capacity to engage old loaf

indicators.note: the capacity word engages, holds within it, the letter for old

parts.note: Joe Biden is American, and liter is the US spelling of litre, a unit of capacity

explanation.surface: A US president's notion of how much a loaf holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like bread; it is the verb, to idle.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to hang about idly, which is to linger aimlessly.
